claim: ALVINN used camera and laser range finder inputs and learned road-following steering behavior from simulated road images and driving examples.
notes: Used as an early representative example, not claimed as the first imitation-learning system.

claim: DAgger treats sequential imitation learning as an online learning problem and aggregates expert labels on states induced by the learner policy.
notes: Guarantees depend on the no-regret learner and reduction assumptions; the article does not claim unconditional safety.

claim: Inverse reinforcement learning infers a reward function under which the observed expert behavior is optimal or near-optimal.
locator: Ng & Russell, ICML 2000; Abstract and Section 2
notes: Reward functions are generally non-identifiable without additional assumptions.

claim: Maximum-entropy IRL defines a globally normalized probabilistic distribution over decision sequences and uses entropy to represent ambiguity in demonstrated behavior.
locator: Ziebart et al., AAAI 2008; Abstract and model formulation
notes: The displayed trajectory proportionality in the article omits the normalizing partition function and environment dynamics for intuition.

claim: GAIL connects imitation learning to GAN-style adversarial training and matches learner and expert occupancy measures with an entropy-regularized objective.
notes: The article defines D(s,a) as the probability that a state-action pair came from the expert; equivalent papers may reverse discriminator labels.

claim: Diffusion Policy represents a visuomotor policy as a conditional denoising diffusion process and uses receding-horizon control for action sequences.
locator: Chi et al., RSS 2023; Abstract and method
notes: The article distinguishes the action-generation representation from the source of supervision.

claim: The RSS 2023 Diffusion Policy paper reports a 46.9% average relative performance improvement across 12 tasks and four robot-manipulation benchmarks.
locator: Appendix G, Performance Improvement Calculation; main paper benchmark results
notes: Relative improvement averaged per task; not 46.9 percentage points and not a universal result.

claim: Under an independent constant per-step error probability epsilon, the probability of at least one error in T steps is 1-(1-epsilon)^T.
locator: This article's explicitly simplified interactive probability model; independent-error assumption
notes: Teaching calculation only; not a general theorem or a measured BC failure rate.

claim: The two-axis taxonomy separates the source of learning signal from the policy representation.
locator: Zheng et al., TNNLS 2024; survey taxonomy, synthesized with primary papers
notes: Repository-oriented conceptual synthesis; axes are not mutually exclusive. DAgger is a data-aggregation/update procedure, not a policy representation.

claim: The 2024 demonstration-learning survey reviews method categories, workflow stages, benchmarks and evaluation practices.
locator: Correia & Alexandre, Robotics and Autonomous Systems 182 (2024), 104812; Abstract
notes: Used to motivate evaluation beyond training loss.

claim: The 2025 legged-robot imitation-learning survey reviews behavior cloning, adversarial motion priors, diffusion methods and deployment challenges.
locator: Mirza & Singh, Frontiers in Robotics and AI (2025); Abstract and taxonomy
notes: Domain-specific survey; not generalized to all robot-learning tasks.

claim: The six diagrams and interactive error calculation are independently authored teaching material, not reproduced paper figures or experimental results.
locator: Article figures and explicitly labeled toy model
notes: SVGs explain conceptual mechanisms; the toy model is not a benchmark reproduction.

claim: The Python module implements continuous BC MSE, DAgger dataset aggregation and a simplified cumulative-error probability calculation.
notes: Pure Python deterministic teaching functions; no robot dynamics, model training or benchmark claim.
